millions of offerings Jagannātha makes tasting

196By custom, food is offered to Jagannātha at that place, and He tastes millions of offerings.61

জগন্নাথের ছোট-বড়, যত ভক্তগণ ৷
নিজ-নিজ উত্তম-ভোগ করে সমর্পণ ॥ ১৯৭ ॥

jagannāthera choṭa-baḍa yata bhakta-gaṇa
of Jagannātha humble and great all the devotees
nija-nija uttama-bhoga kare samarpaṇa
each his own the best food make offering

197All of Jagannātha’s devotees, humble and great, offered Him the best food they had.

রাজা, রাজমহিষীবৃন্দ, পাত্র, মিত্রগণ ৷
নীলাচলবাসী যত ছোট বড় জন ॥ ১৯৮ ॥

rājā, rāja-mahiṣī-vṛnda, pātra, mitra-gaṇa
the king the host of queens ministers friends
nīlācala-vāsī yata choṭa-baḍa jana
of Nīlācala the residents all humble and great people

198The king, the queens, the ministers and friends, all the residents of Nīlācala, humble and great,

নানা-দেশের দেশী যত যাত্রিক জন ৷
নিজ-নিজ-ভোগ তাঁহা করে সমর্পণ ॥ ১৯৯ ॥

nānā-deśera deśī yata yātrika jana
of various lands natives all pilgrim people
nija-nija-bhoga tām̐hā kare samarpaṇa
each his own food there make offering

199and all the pilgrims from many lands offered their own food there.

আগে-পাছে, দুই পার্শ্বে উদ্যানের বনে ৷
যেই যাহা পায়, লাগায়, — নাহিক নিয়মে ॥ ২০০ ॥

āge-pāche, dui pārśve udyānera vane
in front and behind on both sides of the gardens in the groves
yei yāhā pāya, lāgāya, — nāhika niyame
whoever whatever (place) finds offers there is no rule

200In front and behind, on both sides, in the groves of the gardens, each offered his food wherever he found a place; there was no fixed rule.

ভোগের সময় লোকের মহা-ভিড় হৈল ৷
নৃত্য ছাড়ি’ মহাপ্রভু উপবনে গেল ॥ ২০১ ॥

bhogera samaya lokera mahā bhiḍa haila
of the offering at the time of people a great crowd formed
nṛtya chāḍi’ mahāprabhu upavane gela
the dance leaving Mahāprabhu into a garden went

201At the time of the offering a great crowd gathered, so Mahāprabhu stopped dancing and went into a garden.62

প্রেমাবেশে মহাপ্রভু উপবন পাঞা ৷
পুষ্পোদ্যানে গৃহপিণ্ডায় রহিলা পড়িয়া ॥ ২০২ ॥

premāveśe mahāprabhu upavana pāñā
absorbed in love Mahāprabhu the garden reaching
puṣpodyāne gṛha-piṇḍāya rahilā paḍiyā
in the flower garden on a house’s raised platform remained lying

202Absorbed in love, Mahāprabhu entered the flower garden and lay down there on the raised platform (piṇḍā) of a house.

নৃত্য-পরিশ্রমে প্রভুর দেহে ঘন ঘর্ম্ম ৷
সুগন্ধি শীতল-বায়ু করেন সেবন ॥ ২০৩ ॥

nṛtya-pariśrame prabhura dehe ghana gharma
from the exertion of dancing the Lord’s on the body heavy sweat
sugandhi śītala-vāyu karena sevana
fragrant cool breeze He makes enjoying

203After the exertion of the dance His body was covered with sweat, and He enjoyed the cool, fragrant breeze.

যত ভক্ত কীর্ত্তনীয়া আসিয়া আরাম ৷
প্রতিবৃক্ষতলে সবে করেন বিশ্রাম ॥ ২০৪ ॥

yata bhakta kīrtanīyā āsiyā ārāma
all the devotees kīrtana singers coming to the garden
prati-vṛkṣa-tale sabe karena viśrāma
under each tree all make rest

204All the devotees and kīrtana singers came into the garden and rested under the trees.

এই ত’ কহিল প্রভুর মহাসংকীর্ত্তন ৷
জগন্নাথের আগে যৈছে করিল নর্ত্তন ॥ ২০৫ ॥

ei ta’ kahila prabhura mahā-saṅkīrtana
thus I have told of the Lord the great saṅkīrtana
jagannāthera āge yaiche karila nartana
before Jagannātha how He did dancing

205Thus I have told of the Lord’s great saṅkīrtana and how He danced before Jagannātha.

রথাগ্রেতে প্রভু যৈছে করিলা নর্ত্তন ৷
শ্রীচৈতন্যাষ্টকে রূপ-গোসাঞি কর্য্যাছে বর্ণন ॥ ২০৬ ॥

rathāgrete prabhu yaiche karilā nartana
in front of the chariot the Lord how did dancing
śrī caitanyāṣṭake rūpa-gosāñi karyāche varṇana
in the Śrī Caitanyāṣṭaka Rūpa Gosāñi has made a description

206How the Lord danced in front of the chariot, Rūpa Gosāñi has described in his Śrī Caitanyāṣṭaka:

রথারূঢ়স্যারাদধিপদবি নীলাচলপতে-
রদভ্রপ্রেমোর্ম্মিস্ফুরিতনটনোল্লাসবিবশঃ ৷
সহর্ষং গায়দ্ভিঃ পরিবৃত-তনুর্বৈষ্ণবজনৈঃ
স চৈতন্যঃ কিং মে পুনরপি দৃশোর্যাস্যতি পদম্ ॥ ২০৭ ॥

rathārūḍhasyārād adhipadavi nīlācala-pater
of the One seated on the chariot near on the main road of Nīlācala of the Lord
adabhra-premormi-sphurita-naṭanollāsa-vivaśaḥ
by abundant waves of love throbbing by the joy of dancing overwhelmed
sa-harṣaṁ gāyadbhiḥ parivṛta-tanur vaiṣṇava-janaiḥ
joyfully by those singing surrounded in body by the Vaiṣṇavas
sa caitanyaḥ kiṁ me punar api dṛśor yāsyati padam
that Caitanya will my again even of the eyes come into the path

207“Before the Lord of Nīlācala, who sits on His chariot on the great road, He dances, overwhelmed by the joy of a dance that throbs with abundant waves of love, while the Vaiṣṇavas around Him sing in delight. Will that Caitanya ever again come before my eyes?” (Stava-mālā, First Caitanyāṣṭaka, 7)63

ইহা যেই শুনে সেই শ্রীচৈতন্য পায় ৷
সুদৃঢ় বিশ্বাস-সহ প্রেমভক্তি হয় ॥ ২০৮ ॥

ihā yei śune sei śrī caitanya pāya
this who hears he Śrī Caitanya attains
sudṛḍha viśvāsa-saha prema-bhakti haya
firm faith with loving devotion arises

208Whoever hears this attains Śrī Caitanya, and loving devotion with firm faith awakens in him.

শ্রীরূপ-রঘুনাথ-পদে যার আশ ৷
চৈতন্যচরিতামৃত কহে কৃষ্ণদাস ॥ ২০৯ ॥

śrī rūpa-raghunātha-pade yāra āśa
Śrī Rūpa’s, Raghunātha’s at the feet whose hope
caitanya-caritāmṛta kahe kṛṣṇadāsa
“Caitanya-caritāmṛta” narrates Kṛṣṇadāsa

209Praying at the feet of Śrī Rūpa and Śrī Raghunātha, I, Kṛṣṇadāsa, narrate the Caitanya-caritāmṛta.64

The Kṣetra-māhātmya calls them Śabaras: the Deity Nīla-mādhava, who later became Jagannātha, once dwelt among the Śabaras, and so they were given the right of intimate service.

  13. Anubhāṣya: during anavasara Jagannātha enjoyed pastimes with Mahā-Lakṣmī in seclusion, keeping the proper majesty (maryādā); now, with her consent, He went out for free pastimes to please the devotees of the path of anurāga, who are devoted to Kṛṣṇa alone, and here the mood of lawful wedlock (svakīyā) recedes.
  14. Anubhāṣya: the sand was like that of the Yamunā’s bank, and the groves on both sides of the road were like those of Vṛndāvana.
  15. Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya: the cowherds (goālās) of Utkala are called gauḍas.
  16. Heading in the edition: “First, honour to the elders.”

  19. Anubhāṣya: this Haridāsa is perhaps the elder Haridāsa (the commentator adds a question mark).
  20. Anubhāṣya: this Haridāsa is perhaps the younger Haridāsa (with a question mark), as distinct from the Haridāsa of the second group (39).
  21. Anubhāṣya: this group went on the left side of the chariot.
  22. Acyutānanda is the son of Advaita Ācārya. Anubhāṣya: this group was made up of Advaita’s followers and went on the right side of the chariot.
  23. Anubhāṣya: the group from Khaṇḍa went behind the chariot.
  24. Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya: just as in the rāsa dance and at His wedding with the queens Śrī Kṛṣṇa manifested Himself at once in many forms (prakāśa), so Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, showing the same power, manifested Himself in every group.
  25. Heading in the edition: “Seeing this, the king is amazed.”
  26. In the original, curi (“theft”) — the Lord’s secret, stealthy pastime. Heading in the edition: “The king silently exchanges signs with Sārvabhauma.”
  27. Anubhāṣya: Jagannātha, amazed at Mahāprabhu’s dancing and singing, stopped His chariot, and Mahāprabhu delighted Jagannātha by dancing before Him. Though the seer and the seen are here one and the same Reality, this wondrous secret was revealed in the variety of the pastimes, and by Mahāprabhu’s mercy the king understood it, and understood too that the Lord’s presence in all seven groups at once was part of the same secret.
  28. Anubhāṣya: playing the role of an ācārya, the Lord openly showed aversion even to the word “king”, yet in secret He was so merciful to Pratāparudra that the king entered into the mystery of His intimate pastimes. The meaning of this play, in which the Lord acts both as Īśvara and as if He were a jīva, no one but His one-pointed devotees can understand.
  29. Anubhāṣya: the Lord was so absorbed in the bliss of dancing and singing that He seemed to have forgotten Himself completely; but as soon as He wished, His potency of will (icchā-śakti), a form of the svarūpa-śakti, manifested His prakāśa forms and so served her Lord.
  30. Anubhāṣya: the Bhāgavatam testifies that at the rāsa dance and at the wedding with the queens Kṛṣṇa appeared in many forms at once; so too Gaurasundara appeared in many forms before the seven kīrtana groups and before Pratāparudra. Only devotees are allowed to see His transcendental pastimes.
  31. Heading in the edition: “By His dance the Lord delivers the people.”
  32. Heading in the edition: the verse is quoted in the Padyāvalī (108) as the words of Mukundadeva.
  33. Heading in the edition: “Glory to the transcendental, ever-new Kāmadeva.” Anubhāṣya: kāma-deva here is transcendental loving desire, which He kindles with His beautiful smile; deva means “transcendental”: this kāma is His own self-luminous nature. The women of Vrajapura are the women of Vraja and of the cities (Mathurā and Dvārakā), full of anurāga.
  34. Heading in the edition: the verse was spoken by Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya and is quoted in the Padyāvalī (74). Anubhāṣya: “I” here is the soul, the jīva, by its own nature; it identifies itself neither with a varṇa nor with an āśrama, but is established in service to the servants of the Vaiṣṇavas.
  35. Anubhāṣya: a burning coal whirled very fast looks like a solid ring of fire, though there is no ring; so Mahāprabhu, dancing wildly, was one, yet He was seen everywhere.
  36. Anubhāṣya: “mighty” (mahā-bala) — Śrī Baladeva. So that the crowd would not crush Mahāprabhu, He was surrounded by three rings: if the crowd broke the third, the second would protect the Lord, and after it the first.
  37. Heading in the edition: “[Śrīvāsa] slaps Haricandana, who becomes angry.”
  38. Heading in the edition: “Even an insult or a blow from a Vaiṣṇava is a sign of good fortune.”
  39. Anubhāṣya: “jaja gaga” — so indistinctly did the Lord’s words sound when He tried to say “Jagannātha”.
  40. The same song as Madhya 1.55; translation as there.   41. pāche pāche yāya, “goes back, back”: facing Jagannātha (116–117), the Lord moved backwards before the chariot; cf. 118 and the Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya there.
  42. Amṛta-pravāha-bhāṣya: when Gauracandra, acting out the song, walked backwards, Jagannātha stood still; when Gaura went forward, Jagannātha slowly moved after Him. Heading in the edition: “In the Lord, enriched with Śrī Rādhā’s mood, there is more prema than in Kṛṣṇa.”
  43. Anubhāṣya: in Śrī Rādhā’s mood Mahāprabhu draws Jagannātha — Kṛṣṇa — from Nīlācala, the place of His pastimes of majesty, to Guṇḍicā, the land of His pastimes of sweetness. He falls back to dispel the doubt whether Kṛṣṇa is really going out of love for Śrī Rādhā and the other people of Vraja; Jagannātha, understanding His mood, stops and waits, and when Gaura goes forward, follows Him, abashed. In this contest of feelings Mahāprabhu, enriched with Śrī Rādhā’s mood — that is, His prema — proves the stronger.
  44. The same verse as Madhya 1.58; translation as there. The heading in the edition says that the verse is cited in the Kāvya-prakāśa (1.4), the Sāhitya-darpaṇa (ch. 1) and the Padyāvalī (382).

  46. Anubhāṣya: a worldly person calls “mind” the heart that makes and unmakes resolves; but the heart that has given up the urge to enjoy and is devoted to Kṛṣṇa’s service Rādhā knows as “Vṛndāvana”, the place of Śrī Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes.
